players.name: António João Pereira de Albuquerque Tavares da Silva

1.headline: Haaland captains everywhere, João Pedro refuses to be left out — Patrick tops the pile by four points
1.introduction: Gameweek 1 and we somehow managed a week of small margins, wasted benches and the strangest thing: almost everyone owned João Pedro. There were squeakers, a proper thrashing and more captains picking Haaland than you could shake a penalty at. Here’s the damage.

matches.title: Richard 56 — Prince Majid Rd FC 57
matches.text: Rich Sutton made the trip to a one‑point defeat after a characteristically tidy 56. Both managers trusted Bruno Fernandes as captain, which produced a heroic four points apiece — proof that two managers can agree on nonsense. João Pedro did the heavy lifting for both sides with 11, but Rami’s Kiernan Dewsbury‑Hall (11) nudged Prince Majid Rd FC over the line. Brutal one‑point losses are why Rich drinks alone.

matches.title: Humorous Name United 72 — Roped in again 71
matches.text: The highest‑scoring game of the week and utterly maddening for Paul. Rob’s 72 just about edged Paul’s brilliant 71 — the sort of result that makes both men simultaneously smug and furious. Rob’s captain gamble on Bruno yielded a meek 4, while Paul had Haaland for 4; neither captain saved the day, but both teams had enough spread scoring (João Pedro again on 11) to turn this into a proper thriller. Paul will complain about a referee that doesn’t exist.

matches.title: Change Name FC 67 — Bielsa's Babes 76
matches.text: Patrick’s 76 was the week’s high score and it was enough to see off Dave’s 67. Both managers went with Haaland as captain and received the same laughably small return (4) — which just goes to show you can’t blame a captain every week. Patrick’s midfield returns (including Ødegaard on 11 and João Pedro on 11) did the trick; David’s team was decent but nine points short. Patrick will now buy a martini to celebrate; he was already halfway there.

matches.title: el Guapo 47 — BeLucky Again 51
matches.text: Tom had the low score of the week with 47 — a rough start for el Guapo. He bravely captained Haaland and received an emphatic four points for his trouble, while Kevin (BeLucky Again) squeaked home with 51. Tom had a 9 on the bench (Granit Xhaka) that never saw the light of day, which will be the only thing he moans about besides Spurs. Kev strolls off with the win and probably another golf round booked.

matches.title: FC Dangerous 50 — Seattle Scorchers 50
matches.text: A perfectly symmetrical draw. Rob Watson and Andrew Crystal both finished on 50 — and both captained Haaland for precisely the same, underwhelming return (4). Martin Ødegaard and João Pedro (11 apiece between the teams) kept things even. A draw that feels like a slow‑burn punch — neither manager will be happy, but at least they can share the bitterness.

matches.title: ChampagneSuperRovers 55 — Atletico Waspo 59
matches.text: Ben Foster’s 59 nudged James Dunne’s 55. James had Granit Xhaka’s nine points sitting on the bench doing absolutely nothing, a rookie sin that cost him edge in what was otherwise a respectable showing. Ben’s team was efficient enough — João Pedro again popping up with 11 — while James will be kicking himself for not dragging Xhaka into the starting XI.

matches.title: Woolbrohampton 71 — Turf Less 50
matches.text: Ben Woolman put the hammer down with the biggest winning margin of the week (21) to make Turf Less the Wednesday evening patsy. Woolly’s 71 felt clinical and comfortable; Martyn Bradshaw’s Turf Less, despite a 13 from Cole Palmer, could not rescue the day. Martyn can blame Burnley for his mood if he likes — it’s the natural response.

awards.text: 72–71 is the kind of result that gives you tinnitus. Rob wins the week’s tightest thriller and gets to enjoy his tea for exactly one more minute before Paul moans about luck.

awards.award: The ‘Spent a Fortune on the Bench’ Award
awards.text: James left Granit Xhaka’s nine points and other useful bits warming the bench for a 55. That’s nine points that could’ve made his life easier — instead they judged him from afar.
Biggest margin of the week (21). Ben delivered a comfortable 71 and left Turf Less wondering what modern life even is.
Tom’s 47 is the week’s low. He also had a 9 on the bench and a captain who scored like a loaf of bread — an all‑round Spursy start to the season.

1.table_commentary: Using the league points and total FPL points tie‑breaker, Patrick’s Bielsa’s Babes sit top after that 76, with Rob (Humorous Name United) in second on 72 and Ben Woolman’s Woolbrohampton third on 71. Ben Foster’s Atletico Waspo and Rami’s Prince Majid Rd FC round out the winning managers; Kevin’s BeLucky Again sneaks into the top half despite a modest total. Mid‑table is the twin‑peak 50s draw between Rob Watson and Andrew Crystal. At the wrong end, Paul, Rich, James, Tom, David and Martyn are staring at 0 H2H points — Tom’s 47 leaves el Guapo rock bottom. In short: a spread of results, a lot of João Pedro sightings and no one has yet built an unassailable lead.

preview.fixture: Prince Majid Rd FC (Rami) vs Woolbrohampton (Ben Woolman)
preview.text: Rami’s 57 faces Woolly’s 71 next. Rami will be hoping his opening win wasn’t just a honeymoon; Ben Woolman already showed he can win big, so this looks like a ‘did you buy the team or not’ test for Rami. Expect Rami to bring the flair and Ben to bring the ruthless consistency.

preview.fixture: Bielsa's Babes (Patrick) vs Humorous Name United (Rob Wilkinson)
preview.text: A tasty rematch of last week’s high scorers. Patrick beat David by nine; Rob scraped past Paul by one. Both managers showed they can put up numbers, so this is likely to be another shootout. Patrick will fancy his chances, but Rob has that one‑point edge in confidence now.

preview.fixture: Turf Less (Martyn Bradshaw) vs ChampagneSuperRovers (James Dunne)
preview.text: Martyn needs to stop being Turf Less and start being Turf More. James will want revenge for leaving points on the bench. Two managers who need points meet — perfect recipe for a nervy Sunday. Martyn will be quietly hoping Cole Palmer has another big day; James will be praying his substitutions remember how to work.

1.closing: Gameweek 1 done. Plenty to moan about, a couple of managers already smug and one or two people with real work to do. Make your transfers, adjust your captains and above all stop leaving decent players on the bench — unless that’s your idea of modern art. See you next week.
